title: GSAP Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the GSAP course.

entries.name: Move to a new position
entries.summary: A tween changes values over time. gsap.to starts from the current value and moves toward the value you give it.

entries.name: Start from a chosen value
entries.summary: gsap.from starts with the supplied values and moves to the element's current values.

entries.name: Set both ends explicitly
entries.summary: fromTo names both the starting and ending values.

entries.name: Choose an easing curve
entries.summary: Easing changes the speed during a tween.

entries.name: Repeat and return
entries.summary: repeat adds more plays after the first. yoyo reverses the direction on alternate plays.

entries.name: Sequence steps on a timeline
entries.summary: A timeline groups tweens in order. By default, a new tween begins after the previous one finishes.

entries.name: Overlap timeline steps
entries.summary: A timeline position can make two tweens overlap.

entries.name: Stagger a group
entries.summary: Stagger starts similar tweens at slightly different times.

entries.name: Control playback
entries.summary: A tween object has methods to play, pause and reverse.

entries.name: Respect reduced motion
entries.summary: GSAP matchMedia can choose different motion based on a media query.

entries.name: Clean up a component animation
entries.summary: A GSAP context can collect animations created for a component.

entries.name: Animate transforms with a purpose
entries.summary: Transform and opacity animations often avoid redoing page layout.
